g.text: Choosing a database — the questions that actually decide it
Work down the list. Most systems stop at the first box.
Do you know all your access patterns up front,
Does anything need a multi-row invariant?
Is a single node genuinely too small?
Now scale is a real reason
Try all of this before either answer
Read replicas · caching · connection pooling · better indexes
federation by feature · a bigger box
Each is reversible. Sharding and a datastore migration are not.
The bar is higher than people think
Modern Postgres on one large instance handles tens of thousands of
writes/s and terabytes of data. Most interview systems — and most
real ones — never leave that envelope.
